data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2022 the syndicate's gross claims outstanding were $184.618m. During 2022 the syndicate reports an overall adverse reestimation of prior year reserves of $2.438m (a strengthening). The report cites a number of influences including reinsurance movements (an external RITC adjustment), heightened inflation and geopolitical events (notably the war in Ukraine) and catastrophe exposure (e.g. Hurricane Ian). The syndicate's book is dominated by reinsurance acceptances which are the most material source of reserve movements. The prior year development figure cited in the report is explicit but RITC activity means gross development allocation across underwriting years is distorted.
raw_causal_phrases: In 2022, there has been an overall deterioration of $2,438k on prior year reserves (2021: deficit $2,626k).

There have been significant changes to price inflation in 2022 due to the war in Ukraine as well as supply side issues caused by covid (amongst other factors). Inflation has increased sharply for all economies, and most forward-looking inflation forecasts suggest high levels of inflation in the short term before reverting to previously observed averages over the longer term.

data.data_quality_notes: Primary opening reserve taken from balance sheet closing 2021 gross claims outstanding. Prior year development: report explicitly states an "overall deterioration of $2,438k" which has been used as the prior-year movement (strengthening). A large External RITC (GBP 101,597k) is recorded in the technical provisions movement which distorts gross development and makes the claims development triangle unreliable as a standalone source; a gross triangle exists but is affected by RITC. The prior year movement cited in the narrative does not explicitly state whether it is gross or net - treated as the authoritative movement per the report but users should note it may be net of reinsurance. Where per-line movements are not provided, LOB allocations are not quantified.
